skill.name: Add detail after the noun (with a phrase or clause)
skill.why: Some details are too big to fit in front of a noun, so you hook them on after it to show the reader exactly which one you mean.
skill.how: Add a phrase (the dog with muddy paws) or a clause with its own verb (the dog that ate my lunch) straight after the noun. Keep the detail right next to the noun it's about.

lines: Sometimes the detail I need won't fit in front of a noun. So I add it after.
The wombat with the sore paw. 'With the sore paw' is a phrase. It tells you which wombat.
The wombat that dug under the fence. That detail has its own verb, dug, so it's a clause.
Either way, the detail goes right after the noun it's about. Move it and the sentence goes wobbly.
